objective: Create and extend LVM physical volumes, volume groups and logical volumes, growing the filesystem with them
secondaryObjectives: Troubleshoot disk space problems, including deleted files still held open and inode exhaustion
Create, check and repair ext4 and XFS filesystems and troubleshoot mount failures
Monitor storage performance with iostat, iotop and df, and identify a saturated device

sources.cite: Linux Foundation Certified System Administrator (LFCS): Domains & Competencies, Storage 20%
sources.note: Relevant text: Storage, 'Configure and manage LVM storage'; 'Create, manage, and troubleshoot filesystems'; Essential Commands, 'Troubleshoot diskspace issues'. Read as the page's HTML on 2026-11-14 (page last modified 2026-10-30).

Relevant text: vgextend: 'If the specified PVs have not yet been initialized with pvcreate, vgextend will initialize them.' pvcreate(8): 'Repeating the force option (-ff) will forcibly create a PV, overriding checks that normally prevent it, e.g. if the PV is already in a VG.' Read in full 2026-11-14.

Relevant text: 'lvextend extends the size of an LV. This requires allocating logical extents from the VG's free physical extents.' -r|--resizefs: 'Resize underlying filesystem together with the LV using fsadm(8).' Read in full 2026-11-14.

Relevant text: 'The filesystem must be mounted to be grown'; shrinking is limited ('Only shrinking the last AG without removing it is implemented'). Read in full 2026-11-14. That resize2fs refuses an XFS filesystem follows from resize2fs being the ext2/3/4 resizer; its exact error text is authored.

brief.situation: You administer db2, the PostgreSQL server at Okanogan Orchards (fictional). Monitoring says /var/lib/pgsql is 97% full. At 10:30 the nightly orchard-import job loads about 2G of harvest data, which will not fit. The cloud team attached a new 50G disk an hour ago. Give the database room without stopping it and without risking the data already there.
handover: /var/lib/pgsql is an XFS filesystem on the logical volume vg_data/lv_pg.
The database must stay up; nobody wants a maintenance window today.
howItWorks: Run commands from the command line: type one, or pick it from the suggestions or the action list. Only this lab's commands run; there is no free shell, and each command's arguments are fixed.
Each command takes operator time: run it, then let it finish, which moves the clock by the minutes it takes. The outage keeps developing on the same clock.
The map shows each host, disk or service and the links between them, with a status in words. Output appears in the terminal as it happens.
When you declare the service restored, you write the incident record and explain your reasoning.

source.note: How many operator minutes each command takes, and when the fictional outage spreads, are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values. The import starts at 10:30, 25 minutes after the start.

writeup.question: For the change record: why the volume could not simply be extended, what you did in which order, and how you know the database has room now.

parts.label: Cause
parts.criteria: Says the 20G filesystem was nearly full and vg_data had no free extents, so lvextend alone had nothing to allocate; the new disk had to join the volume group first.
parts.modelAnswer: vgs showed vg_data with 0 free, so there were no extents to give the logical volume. The new 50G disk /dev/vdc had to become a physical volume in vg_data first.

parts.label: Steps
parts.criteria: pvcreate (optional) and vgextend with /dev/vdc, then lvextend -r (or lvextend then xfs_growfs on the mount point); never pvcreate on /dev/vdb, never resize2fs on XFS; all online.
parts.modelAnswer: pvcreate /dev/vdc, vgextend vg_data /dev/vdc, lvextend -r -L +30G vg_data/lv_pg, which grew the XFS filesystem with the volume while mounted. /dev/vdb was never touched.

parts.label: Proof
parts.criteria: Shows df -h /var/lib/pgsql with the new size (and vgs/lvs), not only the lvextend message.
parts.modelAnswer: df -h now shows 50G with 39% used, so the 10:30 import's 2G fits.

metadataWiped.label: Overwrote the volume group's disk
metadataWiped.narrative: pvcreate -ff wrote a new label over /dev/vdb, which held vg_data. The database runs for now, but the volume group will not come back at the next reboot without a metadata restore.

importFailed.narrative: orchard-import failed with No space left on device at 10:30.

stillFull.narrative: The filesystem was still 20G and 97% full when the change was closed.

expertPath.text: df -h /var/lib/pgsql (97%), vgs vg_data (0 free), lsblk (vdc is the new empty disk).
lvextend -r -L +30G vg_data/lv_pg grows the volume and the XFS filesystem online.
df -h /var/lib/pgsql shows 50G; record the change and an alert threshold for next time.

fixed.headline: Good: grown online, in order
fixed.body: You checked where the space could come from, added only the new disk, and grew the volume and filesystem together without stopping the database.

fixedGaps.headline: Room made, with gaps
fixedGaps.body: The database has room. The criteria show what it cost: time, a change before the evidence, a second step, or the wrong tool tried first.

metadataWiped.headline: The volume group's disk was relabeled
metadataWiped.body: -ff overrides the check that /dev/vdb is already in a VG. Only the empty disk (lsblk shows vdc with nothing on it) should be initialized.

importFailed.headline: The import ran out of space
importFailed.body: vgs and lsblk show in two minutes that the space must come from vdc; the whole change takes about ten.

stillFull.headline: Closed too soon
stillFull.body: Check df before you close: an extended logical volume is not a bigger filesystem until the filesystem grows too.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No record was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: A full filesystem on LVM with no free extents in the volume group needs a new physical volume first. Confirm with df, vgs and lsblk; pvcreate /dev/vdc and vgextend vg_data /dev/vdc; then lvextend -r -L +30G vg_data/lv_pg so the XFS filesystem grows with the volume while mounted; prove it with df. Never touch the disk already in the group, and use xfs_growfs, not resize2fs, for XFS.
